W3 (cost lens), after E028.

**Tip (E027).** E026 recipe at 8.75 true epochs (219 steps at batch 2000). Resolution split 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%. Measured 5.878 s at 0.7547 on seeds 0–2. My estimate of the true mean is about 0.752–0.7535, so it sits on the bar. Each epoch cut re-rolls the RNG streams, which makes seeds 0–2 a lottery around a slowly falling mean.

**Time budget:** time ≈ F + V × (pixel-weighted steps), with F ≈ 0.5 s.
- A uniform cut of 0.25 epoch saves about 0.14 s. The measured E026→E027 drop was 0.14 s for 6 steps, about 0.023 s per step.
- One step costs about 0.032 s at 32 px and about 0.016 s at 20 px.
- Systematic bias: I over-forecast time 7 times out of the last 12. Every structural saving came out larger than my pixel or MAC model. E028's FreezeOut gave −0.52 s against my −0.12 s, so backward work and memory traffic on the high-res layers dominate more than I assumed. Correction: when I estimate a saving, multiply it by about 1.5. Anchor to the tip and shade forecasts low.
- MAC cuts on small maps return about half their share (E021). Cuts on high-res work return more than their share (E026, E028).

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epochs: about 1.5–2.5 s/pp.
- 20 px phase: about 1+ s/pp (noisy).
- FreezeOut: about 0.5 s for about 0.3 pp, so roughly 1.7 s/pp. That is competitive, but there is no margin to spend.
- Every lever so far trades at roughly 1.5–2 s/pp. No free lunch has appeared.

**Binding constraint: margin.** We need time-neutral gains of at least 0.2 pp. LS, wd, lr, Muon lr, the alpha ramp and the final LR all came back flat or within noise (E009, E013, E014, E016, E022, E025).

**Mechanisms:**
1. Lookahead endpoint averaging: about 1 pp (E005). A harder pull hurts (E025).
2. Muon: about +0.66 pp (E006). Its lr is flat. Filters are renormalized, so filter wd is inert.
3. Accuracy is built in the 28/32 px phases (E011, E018, E024). The earliest phase is cheap to degrade (E026).
4. Last-group width matters (E010).
5. RNG stream × seed effects are about ±0.3–0.4 pp at the 3-seed mean level.

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp.
- Time noise is about 1%.
- Deltas under 0.25 pp cannot be resolved without held-out seeds.

**Unsure:**
- Loss-based example dropping vs a uniform cut. My prior is that it roughly matches a uniform cut, slightly better or worse depending on the LS interaction.
- Per-resolution whitening. The eigenvector sign and order can differ across resolutions, which could jolt group 1 at each switch. Unless it is aligned, it is a risk.
- PCIe transfer of the margin.

forecasts.reason: About 9% fewer steps saves about 0.4 s. Dropping the easy 10% under LS 0.3 likely costs about as much as an epoch cut (about 0.3 pp), so the trade is roughly epoch-dial parity.
The averaging knobs have been flat (E025 aside). Halving the reset frequency saves a few foreach ops and likely leaves accuracy within noise, short of +0.15 pp.
LS has been flat (E013). Removing it late may sharpen logits but rarely helps top-1 under averaging, so +0.15 pp is unlikely.
It repeats E026's swap, which saved about 0.18 s and probably clears the 2.5% time cut. The accuracy cost of 0.0–0.2 pp is unresolvable on 3 seeds, and the RNG stream is unchanged.

Eigenbasis sign and order flips across resolutions shock group 1 at each switch unless aligned. Even if aligned, the stem mismatch is minor because BN adapts quickly. Extra eigh and interpolate cost about 0.03 s.

cruxes: What is the E027 tip's held-out seeds 3–12 mean? If it is below 0.752, every time-cutting idea must first buy back margin, and nothing time-neutral has worked so far.

Is any lever better than about 1.5 s/pp? E028's FreezeOut saved 0.52 s for about 0.3 pp. If a milder FreezeOut (last 15%, or group 1 only without the whitening layer) holds accuracy, it beats epochs and the 20 px extension.
Does per-sample loss-based dropping (I044) beat a uniform cut of the same steps by at least 0.15 pp held-out? If it does, it opens a new dial; if not, data-selection ideas are dead.
